text:
The original Archimedes Screw is used primarily for liquids, which is why it has to be installed on an angle, so the pockets of liquid are carried up it. It's operating principle is gravity - each 'glob' of liquid stays in its 'pocket'. (That would also work for a flowing solid like grain etc). As a matter of constructional convenience some very large Archimedes screws e.g. in sewage works, are built with a rotating screw inside a fixed outer casing, but they still use gravity as the operating mechanism.

This elevator looks very similar but the mechanism is quite different, it relies on relative motion between screw and casing and friction within the material being conveyed. As Tom says, there is no difference whether the screw rotates or the casing rotates. (An original Archimedes screw, with the screw fixed to the housing, would not work if stood vertically).
Fascinating though, I'd never seen or heard of this before.
rationale: The user expresses fascination and appreciation for the information provided about the Archimedes Screw and its mechanisms.

text:
review_headline: Windows Freemium review_body: Where to start...no pun intended. I had hope for Windows 10 after hearing people say "it's just like windows 7 it's awesome" my hope was quickly destroyed as soon as I clicked on the "amazing" new start button. You basically have the ugly, useless tile screen from windows 8 put into a box on your desktop, not a true start menu. The start menu is made up of stupid, useless, ugly tile start screen apps, all apps list and if you scroll all the way to the bottom of the list you will find programs and accessories which is the only thing that should be there in the first place.

Microsoft needs to give up on the stupid useless, app garbage on desktops. The search bar next to the "start menu" is laggy and brings up web search results etc. even if you simply search for a file on your pc, the relocation of simple features/settings is dumb and hiding things behind app style Windows 8 junk is not cool.

Cortana sucks, again the search is laggy and to even use it you need to basically let the program monitor your every move and keystroke. Microsoft used to pride itself on respecting users privacy calling out data miners like google but as you may have guessed by reading the revised versions of their user agreement they sent out prior to releasing Windows 10 that is no longer the case. Windows 10 will track your every move or click, apps can read every message or conversation and data mine your entire PC in every nook and cranny including personal files on your hard drive. If you don’t believe it check out the settings on any program you open and see for yourself. You will now see notifications, news stories and ads on your lock screen (what is this a damn phone) and every time you launch the new edge browser you will get MSN top stories/ads. There are literally a hundred options you need to turn off to not have your every click tracked and sent to Microsoft and advertisers...even if you turn them off they are still on in another menu somewhere else, do you understand why it's free...more like freemium.

The new edge browser simply sucks compared to any other browsers out there including internet explorer. When you launch edge it gives you an infinite scrolling screen of MSN news and ads that you cannot turn off, at least I cannot find a way to do it, with a search bar saying "where to next" where you can do a web search with bing. I wanted to change my web search to Yahoo but it required going to yahoo.com then opening then new edge menu bar, and adding it then setting it to default, users on windows 7/8 will have trouble with this as it can be very tricky to find. I didn't find many positives with edge, it loads up decently but what’s the use when you have an a fraction of the options and customizations you have with any other browser and the fact that Edge doesn’t support a lot of websites hence why Windows 10 still has Internet Explorer tucked away. I can draw on the web page I’m looking at....whoopee, it's the app version of internet explorer on Windows 8 with Microsoft paint integration.

The OS feels more like a phone than ever before. If you boot up windows 8.1 then took a windows phone and laid it on the bottom left corner of the pc monitor screen you have Windows 10. It almost runs like an advertising tool for Microsoft to sell you useless crap via tiles and notifications popping up. I tried playing my games that I was running fine on Windows 8.1/7 and there are many issues and graphics issues. Some games like Borderlands/Borderlands 2 have major graphic issues now where bushes and bullets look like paint blotches splattered on the screen no matter how much you play with the video options. Dead Island, Left 4 Dead 2 and Dying Light will not work at all, they simply crash when launched so I’m wondering if my ATI Radeon card is having windows 10 update issues as they worked on 8.1. WOW just stopped working as well, battle.net app freezes and looses track of where the files are stored on my PC, but now works fine since I deleted this Microsoft spyware off my PC and went back to 8.1.

Windows 10 update will override the drivers installed by your graphics card suite causing crashes, graphical problems and infinite restarts if the driver you have installed is not the one big brother has in their auto update. Again I had hopes that Microsoft would actually deliver a quality product like Windows 7 but instead we get a lazy freemium version of windows 8.1 that rivals google it terms of disgusting spying/data stealing for profit. Windows 10 is "freemium" not free, you pay for it by giving up every ounce of privacy for Microsoft’s financial benefit. They baseically turn your PC into a Microsoft server, your PC can also be used to upload updates to other pc users/owners like a hotspot.

I’m glad that I switched to OSX again a few months back and only use windows on my secondary computer, I won’t be putting this garbage on my mac. If you do upgrade the first thing you should do is go into every settings menu you can find and check the privacy options, you will still be data mined just not as badly. You will have to do this more than once as there are for example two control panels....named the same but both with their own privacy settings. The split personality of Windows 8 is back in full effect . In short Windows 10 is just Windows 8.1 freemium edition, you even still have to right click the start menu to get control panel (one of them) and stuff quickly because if you traditionally left click on it, it wil just shows you apps and useless tile garbage, basically the Windows 8 start screen in a box instead of desktop features and shortcuts to things you actually need.

Windows 10 is a total failure, the people claiming it to be Windows Christ are simply dreaming or paid to say so, stick to windows 7/8.1. Windows 10 is nothing like Windows 7, try it first on an old computer if you are curious. If you hate Windows 8, Windows 10 will not improve anything, you will still be using the same failed phone/pc hybrid operating system but you will have to give up ALL your privacy for nothing you can't do on windows 7/8.1. Apparently you will also be paying for games like solitaire (1.49 a month) and 14.99 for a dvd/blue ray play back software. Hopefully anyone can see where this is going.

How can users trust Microsoft when Windows 10 is nothing but SPYWARE? Microsoft's own definition of spyware is posted here [...]. The only way they get around their own definition is the fact that people are still "Accepting" the Privacy Policy to download the software.

•Changing the configuration of your computer
Spyware is often associated with software that displays advertisements (called adware) or software that tracks personal or sensitive information.

review_headline: Down grade from 5 to 1. Blue Screen of Death is Back!!! Regular crashes on all three computers review_body: November 27, 2015

Well, we had a couple of months honeymoon then all hell breaks loose. I have Windows 10 upgrade in three out of four PCs: A Surface Pro 3, a Lenovo Yoga 2, and a Dell All-in-One with an i7 CPU: All less than two years old.

Now:

The Lenovo runs like a dog from time to time--simply slows down to a crawl for no apparent reason. The wi-fi needs a system restart to work every now and then, and attaching an external monitor causes the system to freeze. NONE of these symptoms occurred before the upgrade. Now I run the Yoga 2 as treading on thin ice.

The Surface Pro 3 had the dreaded critical error, saying that the Start Menu had stop and promises to fix it upon restart. Well, it's not fixed and ended up crashing--freezing--the computer. Then I had to reload Windows using a local user account and then recreate my original user account but guess what--all the software had to be reloaded! Caused me some choice swear words and days of my life. THEN, it happened again last week! This time, before it freezes my computer, I use a Windows reload to "repair" the operating system. The Critical Error went away BUT the cover keyboard stopped working altogether. I looked through the Windows support site and the best advise they gave was to totally reload a clean Windows copy and re-install all my programs. I didn't follow the advice and further my search for a solution. After some anxious hours, I found from a user forum (not the Microsoft official site) that I had to perform a "two-button" shut down to re-kickstart the cover keyboard and it worked. Phew!

Now, the Dell desktop: The BSOD (blue screen of death) is back!!! After some software updates, all of a sudden, the system gradually slowed down, and the the BSOD appeared. I used the physical power button to turn it off and on, and it would run for a few minutes. The cycle of slow down to BSOD would repeat. I used my SP3 to download to a USB thumb drive Windows 10 upgrade and booted the PC from the thumb drive using the new clean W10 in the repair mode. After another few hours of anxiety, I got my system running, at least for the time being.

After using XP, 7, and 8.x, I thought the stability that we had enjoyed for a decade would remain, but Windows 10 fails to deliver the promise. I have problems with three of out my three Windows 10 "upgrades". I serious doubt I'm unique.

I have one more HP desktop still running W7. I am not touching that puppy. I need to have at least ONE stable system around!

Original Review is below:

Got my upgrade notice and immediately downloaded from Microsoft and upgraded my Surface Pro 3 with it.
The upgrade experience was seamless. The whole process took less than an hour with no intervention from the user except in the first few minutes to agree to the license agreement, etc. Then the upgrade ran itself, including restarting.
Then we have to select express or custom setup. The express setup essentially sends Microsoft all the data it wants regarding your surfing habits, location, default apps for pictures and videos, music, etc. I selected custom setup and picked and chose what I wanted to share. Again, this was fast and painless.
I'm using the Edge browser on Amazon to type this. It loaded fast and has worked seamlessly so far. However, I can't find a way to use setting to specify my multiple start pages, like all other browsers, and have to add as custom pages one at a time. Irritating.
I was also a tester for the preproduction versions. This is based on my experience with them as well.
The best thing is that Windows is now equally touch and keyboard-mouse friendly. You can have it in tablet mode and maximize the square icons display. You can also resize it to become a squarish start menu that occupies only the lower left corner of the display. The difference is that it shows live feeds such as weather, news, and stock market indices. It's as mouse friendly as it is touch friendly. Nice.
I timed the start up. It took about 12 seconds from pushing the power button on my Surface Pro 3 for the login screen to appear. The wireless took about 15 seconds to connect to my wi-fi. By the time I typed in my password, it's all good to go, 20 seconds or less. The fast start up of W8 was what prompted me to upgrade from W7 to W8 and I'm glad this was retained.
There is a prominent search window next to the Start icon where you can search without having to start a browser.
Next to Search is a Task icon. Clicking it brings all open apps in tiles on the main screen. It's not gimmicky at all and very convenient to switch tasks.
So far everything works as when I was using W8.1. It's as seamless as any Windows upgrade that I had done. No complaints.
Microsoft's goal is to fix the defects of W8 without losing its advantages while adding goodies. Looks like they have hit the mark.

text:
review_headline: Solid Protection for Windows and Android review_body: I am very particular about my security software and I have been researching for the last several months to find a solid solution that doesn’t bring the system to its knees, stays out of the way unless it finds a real problem, protects my system adequately, allows installation on all of my target systems (not just 3) and provides Android protection as well. The last point narrowed my choices significantly. I downloaded several 30-day trials of software packages and after exploring my options I finally settled on Panda Total Security. It provides everything for which I have been looking and I am very pleased with it.

I am a returning customer to Panda, having used them in the past. My last version of Panda security products was the 2009 version which was hard to install and it had a nasty habit of making very large daily backups. Fortunately these issues have been addressed.

In the box is a CD with the installation binary as well as the activation code. I actually do not recommend using the CD, and I will explain that in a moment. To set up for install, I logged into Panda’s website and created my account, then tied the activation code to my account. The account summary screen then showed me several options for setting up my systems to be installed - one for PC, one for Android and one for Mac. Included was a set of instructions for each system type. Also included was a download link for the software. I chose the download and it brought down a current binary and began the installation. Because the download brings down the most current version, I recommend this over the CD install unless you are installing to a system without Internet access when the install takes place (and there are legitimate reasons for that).

Once installed on my laptop, I plugged in my activation code and email address and everything was ready. The install took only a few minutes and was very out of the way.

The interface is a strange animal and is vastly different than the last version I used. It is set up as a tiled interface and somewhat resembles the Windows 8 Metro desktop. I personally do not mind this and I think it’s easy to understand. What I do not like is that it cannot be resized and the client window is a little on the small side for my tastes. I also do not understand why it is not scrollable, instead relying on direction arrows to move to another set of icons.

One of the main elements in any security suite is the firewall. Panda’s firewall has always been top-notch and this version is no exception. It provides all of the protection mechanisms you will want or need, including application control (monitoring outbound connections), port monitoring and blocking, attack detection and more. It is not the easiest firewall to configure and the options are not all grouped together like I would like, but it works well and that’s what’s important.

The antivirus is as I remember it - fast. It also does not gobble up huge amounts of system resources either and I have it running the background as I write this. Looking at the task list the virus scan takes less than 5% of the CPU while it is working which is a big improvement over previous versions and definitely is better than other packages I have tried. So far it has not encountered any issues on my system so I do not know how well it will handle things when it finds a problem; I imagine I will find out at some point.

One thing I have noticed about the antivirus - I found no settings that relate to email scanning. I do not know if this means I have no email protection or if I have no way to configure it. I don’t use Outlook so I do not know if there is a component that integrates. Also, I have seen nothing that suggests the presence of an antispam module. To me this is nothing because I use a dedicated antispam application but to others this might be a real problem. Other more technical reviews online suggest thatPanda includes an antispam module as well as email protection, but I am not sure how to access those settings, so I can’t even turn these features on or off.

There are a number of less critical tools that really add to the value of this package. I especially like the Wi-Fi monitor what tells me at a glance what devices are connected to my network. I like the data protection as well that prevents my personal data and files from leaving without my knowledge. There is a virtual keyboard too to help foil keyloggers. Included is a toolbar for your browser that provides safe searches as well as browser cleanups. I like having a built-in password management solution too - very handy and it keeps everything under one umbrella.

One of the big features I look at in a security suite is the parental controls. I used to really dislike the parental controls in Panda as they required setting up special log-ins and passwords had to be entered after being logged into the system - they were not out-of-site, out-of-mind. That apparently is no longer a problem, and now the controls are tied to the system login. I was able to turn on controls for myself, block a few categories and then went out and tried to access a couple of sites in my chosen categories. I was unceremoniously barred from sites in those categories - the controls work great.

The other part of this suite is the fact that it can also be loaded on Android devices. There is a Mac version too but I do not have a device suitable for it. I have a tablet that runs Android and I decided to load up Panda on it and see how well it would work. I was especially interested in the anti-theft module.

I loaded it the same way as I did on my Windows machine - I logged in to Panda’s website and specified that I wanted to load up the Android version. I was taken to the Play Store, to something other than Panda Mobile Security (it was called Free Antivirus and Security) which was a little confusing, but I downloaded and installed it. I entered the email and activation code as I did on the Windows side and the application converted over to Mobile Security. This was a slightly confusing situation and I would have liked a little heads-up that the free version of Mobile Security had a different name.

Mobile security has a number of nice components including a decent antivirus, privacy checker, task killer and anti-theft module. It is by no means as complete as the Windows application but it does not need to be.

I launched the antivirus and it blazed through the application and file scan in just a few short minutes, completing a scan of almost 20,000 files in under 5 minutes. It found nothing of interest so I am not sure how it will handle things if it manages to find a threat at some point. This is a low-use tablet that does little more that stream music and run the Kindle application so it’s likely I never will need the antivirus.

The Privacy Auditor is an interesting component that looks at all of the applications installed on the system and reports what kinds of access each has. This includes location tracking, access to your online accounts, access to the Bluetooth interface, network access, access storage, ability to change your security settings and a lot more. It also provides a very easy way to eliminate these applications with a single button click.

The task killer is exactly what it sounds like - it gives you the ability to terminate an application and remove it from memory. Many of these applications are necessary for the system to work so it is not advisable to just go in and kill applications without knowing what you’re doing, but it is helpful to bounce out applications that you really don’t need running at the moment, like browsers or Facebook. If you’re running low on memory, this is a good place to look for help.

The anti-theft module is where my interest lies with this package and it gives me a few things. I can use it to locate my device, and in doing so it has pinpointed on the map where it believes my tablet is (apparently it is next door - need to talk to my neighbor about that), it allows me to remotely lock and/or wipe the tablet and it also gives me the ability to get a photo of whoever is using my tablet if they fail to log in. This is exactly what I was looking for and it works as I need it to work. I am not unhappy.

Between the Windows version and the Android version, this is exactly the kind of protection I have been looking for and I am very pleased with it, save for a couple of minor quirks. The firewall and antivirus are solid as usual, and the mobile security gives me the anti-theft functions I need. Because I can load this package on all of my devices and have installations to spare, I didn’t have to spend an outrageous amount of money to get solid protection for everything on my network. This is a good, solid solution and if you need protection for multiple devices that are of varying OS types, this is a great option.using, but I downloaded and installed it. text:
review_headline: A MUST-Have for Digital Photographers review_body: Being relatively new to DSLR photography this is my first experience with Lightroom software. Previously I had used point-and-shoot cameras and made adjustments with Photoshop Elements, which I liked a lot. I resisted Lightroom because I thought PS Elements did everything I could possibly need - I was wrong.

Having joined a digital photography club in an attempt to learn more about my camera, I was surprised at how universally the other, more experienced members, loved and recommended Lightroom. In addition to being a superior tool for organizing photos, Lightroom also allows you to do some nice editing and seems to handle edits to my Canon RAW files better than Elements did. There is also an option to take the files I've been working on in Lightroom and "Edit In" another program, so I can finish them off in Elements. Or, I can just use my favorite filters in Lightroom directly.

In addition to editing, Lightroom makes it easy to watermark your photos and publish them to the internet, including Facebook.

Maybe my favorite feature in Lightroom is the ability to tether the camera to the PC while I'm doing a shoot and see the images in full size. With a full size image on the screen it's so much easier to see if I need to make changes in lighting, position, filters, etc.

Learning and using Lightroom was not intuitive for me, even as someone with years of experience using Adobe's Photoshop Elements. However, there are some fantastic free video tutorials on the Adobe website that can walk you through how to do the basic functions. For experienced Lightroom users there is also a video with detailed outlines of six new features and improvements in Lightroom 5.

Highly recommended to anyone who is trying to move beyond basic point-and-shoot photography and basic edits. star_rating: 5 review_id: RSO4A5EDFE097
rationale: The review provides positive feedback on the software and highly recommends it for digital photographers, expressing satisfaction with its features and benefits

text:
review_headline: ReSpeedr can give very good results. review_body: I recently bought proDAD's video speed modifying software, "ReSpeedr", to try slow-motion with video. I knew from samples I had seen that there were likely to be picture artifacts with this software (and also with a more expensive alternative, "Twixtor"), but it appeared that with care, and with some subjects, results could be at least adequate. But, my first attempts with speed changes of 1/2X, 1/4X, 1/10X, 2X, 4X, and 10X with a difficult video clip were poor, and they indicated that the best results were likely to be with subjects that moved against plain (or at least out of focus) surrounding areas, did not move rapidly through the frame, and did not intersect the frame edges. This unfortunately precluded the use of some subject material that I was looking forward to rendering in slow-motion. I then tried using Sony Vegas to render 60p footage as 30p, slowing it (with the "Velocity" control) to half-speed. This worked fairly well, but I was looking for greater speed changes. On a whim, I tried placing the Vegas 50%-slowed video clip (which had a considerable amount of fine detail in it, and which also had things passing in front of and behind other things) on the ReSpeedr timeline. I set the speed control in ReSpeedr for 1/4 speed for a total speed-change factor of 8 between the two programs. I did not expect much - but I was quite surprised by the final outcome (shown on YouTube). In ReSpeedr I had set the speed to "25%", the "Sub-Frame Mode" to "Optical-Flow", with "Stabilize" selected, with "Rolling-Shutter Compensation" deselected, and with "Use of Original Frame Rate" (29.970fps) selected, and hit "Start". The resulting clip showed slight anomalies at the extreme frame edges and (in a surprisingly minor way) with things passing near other things, but overall the results were very good. I then put the clip back into Vegas and stabilized it again there (at "10%" which further smoothed the motion and it also trimmed off the extreme picture edges, "cleaning" those of artifacts - with a result that retains a considerable level of fine detail in the video (although this is somewhat spoiled by the further compression and transcoding necessary for practical streaming on YouTube). Some "curious" artifacting still remains - but at the level at which it exists here, I do not find it objectionable. The original was shot with a Panasonic G5 (several Panasonic MFT cameras produce very sharp video...), with a Rokinon 7.5mm "fisheye" lens, hand-held (without the aid of braces or handles). I later tried shooting a test using 4K video (shot with a Panasonic GH4 at 30fps) and this also worked well when stabilized, slightly cropped, and then reduced to 1080-30p in Vegas (this is also on YouTube – search my name there to find these samples). Overall, I’m pleased with what I can achieve using ReSpeedr in combination with other programs – although processing time when using the highest quality settings can be rather lengthy, even with the use of a very fast computer. Also, this program is very easy and intuitive to use, a BIG “plus” for me...!;-) I recommend it, especially given its moderate price and (potentially...) very good results.
--DR star_rating: 4 review_id: RKNKCLOCSFU1Y
rationale: The review expresses a high level of satisfaction with ReSpeedr, noting good results and ease of use, while also mentioning minor issues and limitations.

review_headline: ABSOLUTELY WONDERFUL!
review_body: I ABSOLUTELY LOVE YNAB!  It is so simple to use and is "right on the money".  I'm a former Mint user and while it's true that it does not sync to your bank account and track all of your transactions for you, I find that I watch what I spend more closely when I actually have to enter the transactions myself.  The mobile app is an awesome companion for this. It's great to be able to enter a transaction right on the spot at a restaurant or store and that it will sync at home or on my husband's mobile app.  In fact, I run a few separate budgets on YNAB (household / savings allotment / business) and easily switch back and forth between them on both my laptop and my mobile device.  I've never had syncing issues others have mentioned. I've used YNAB for 6 months and still love it.  On Mint I spent as much time correcting mis-categorized or duplicate transactions as I have just entering a transaction on YNAB.  My budget is ALWAYS accurate and keeping it local on my devices makes me feel more secure as well.  The only server I want my financials on is my bank's.  I give it 5 stars because it deserves every bit of it.

text:
review_headline: BEWARE IF YOU'RE CONSIDERING BUYING THIS NERO CLASSIC 2015 - IT DOES NOT DO WHAT IT CLAIMS IT DOES!
review_body: I hate this version.  I purchased this version for burning picture slide DVDs and burning music CDs.  Well, for burning picture slide DVDs this version is a ripoff.  This version does not let you edit your pictures once you've lined them up to burn them.  Also, this part was what took the cake for me.  Adding transitions to my picture slide DVD made me very upset because this version shows me a huge listing of transitions only not to allow me to use them.  I clicked one of the many transitions and it displays a huge message saying that I don't have the transition pack and automatically takes me to the page where I can buy Nero Classic 2015 which is what I have.  As for burning music CDs, that task too is problematic.  The choice for burning CDs the ones you can play on your regular DVD players, this Nero Classic version gives choices only if you want to burn the CD as Jukebox version which will only play on your computer and not on traditional CD players.  Then, burning as MP3 music files, Nero Classic burns the MP3 files on CDs but when I tried playing these, again these would only play on my computer and not on my MP3 boombox.  My boombox plays both traditional music files and MP3 files.  So you see, I'm very upset with Nero.  And to top it, I looked up how to contact them for help.  I found out that they charge $1.29 to help me on the telephone.  Really?  I never expected to have such a hard time with this Nero Classic 2015 software.  I mean, I'm not a computer geek but I always thought I could figure things out on my own.  I mean, I had a previous Nero version for a long time and that version did everything for me.  I loved it.  This is why I purchased this Classic 2015 version because I thought it would be everything I had before in my previous version plus more options.  I was WRONG!  I ended up with more limitations than with any software I had ever worked with.  SO, BEWARE IF YOU'RE CONSIDERING BUYING THIS NERO CLASSIC 2015.  UNLESS YOU'VE ALREADY PLAYED WITH THIS VERSION BEFORE AT A FRIENDS HOUSE, STAY AWAY FROM IT OTHERWISE, YOU'LL BE FRUSTRATED AND UPSET LIKE I AM.      UPDATE:  I just wanted to say that after posting this review here, someone from NERO wrote me through this website to give me a link to download Nero transition pack and another link to correct my 2 major problems I currently have.  Well, I just want to say that I went through the process of downloading per this person's recommendation and absolutely NOTHING happened as a result of this which proves my point.  Something is terribly wrong with this software.  Why isn't everything advertised on NERO CLASSIC 2015 not a true representation of what one gets when purchasing this software??  As I said before, I had an older version of NERO and there was no mystery as to what you could do with this software.  How disappointing to buy this version of NERO CLASSIC 2015 only to find out how inferior it is to previous releases.

text:
review_headline: Organized to Perfection review_body: Kasimdzhanov’s (former World Champion) presentation is very clear, organized, and effective. Whether you want to learn some basic opening ideas to deal with the French Defense, or if you want a serious, well-devised plan for how to deal with a top player’s French, this is DVD is what you are looking for. Volume #1, the first disc in a series of three (sold separately), features the Winawer. Even if you are interested in the French, but not the Winawer, seeking something like a response to black’s classical variation (3. … Nf6), then you can skip this volume and go right to the second. Though connected by numbers, each DVD in this Fritz Trainer series is self-contained.

The main menu page of the Fritz Trainer is particularly well laid out: it has two ways for you to choose from Kasimdzhanov’s videos. The first is simply to follow through the linear progression of Kasimdzhanov’s videos, where he alternates between theory and practical demonstration of the theory. The second is that the main menu page contains the main line in bold (with sidelines not in bold) with the relevant video corresponding to the GM’s discussion of that part of the line and the ideas, as exhibited in practical applications (GM games with recent developments). This second part of the main menu page makes this DVD valuable as a reference resource for future revisits to the material.

Highly recommended, regardless of the player purpose with regard to the French. star_rating: 5 review_id: R2QL6GGNCYXEXT

Assuming it was now in eternal spin, I removed the disc and looked at it. The disc had scrapes, scratches, and FINGERPRINTS on it. text:
review_headline: software
review_body: I needed this product for a laptop that I had reworked. I would have preferred the Professional version of this software but it was not available. I also learned a great lesson from this issue. Anyone who purchases a new computer, laptop, etc., if the product you purchased is Windows operating system, you had better write down the product key for your Windows software and keep up with it. I crashed a computer that was 4 years old and the product key was located on the bottom of my laptop. The computer shop looked for it but it was faded/worn off. I had my whole computer wiped and started all over but I had no product key for my Windows Professional so I had to buy a new one. After my computer guy told me this, I went home and looked at my new HP laptop, wrote the product key down and since the product key was on the bottom of the computer and it was still readable, I placed a piece of scotch tape over the product key so it would not wear off or fade. If I would have known this, I would have wrote down the computer product key from my Toshiba computer and I would not have had to purchase another one. No one has ever told me this and I have many computer products. When you are sold a computer that operates off Windows, you have purchased that product key and if your computer ever crashes, you will need this product key to reset everything. Lesson learned. I saved $20 ordering this software from Amazon because the shop was going to charge me $85 for a new product key.

text:
review_headline: A powerful companion to Adobe Lightroom, and a great deal review_body: As the chief photographer for World View Wallpaper, I demand a lot from my photographs. Shooting on a Canon 6D with the 24-105mm L, I'd been pretty happy with my photographs...until I saw what DxO OpticsPro is capable of.

While there are a lot of enhancement options available, the two biggest ones / the primary reasons for buying OpticsPro are:

1) PRIME noise reduction - essentially, powerful noise reduction with minimal detail loss. I've taken pictures at 64,000 ISO and gotten results that are completely usable for the web. It takes several minutes per photo, so it's not something to be used willy-nilly...but if you /need/ to capture more light, this is the best option available to digital photographers today.
2) Incredible lens correction - Adobe Lightroom does a decent job of correcting for lens distortions, but it's limited by the fact that it's still working with the RAW file you gave it from your camera, which is, despite what you might expect, still compressed. OpticsPro's correction recovers additional details and stores them in an uncompressed file that's about 3x bigger. Again, not something to be used lightly - but if you're a professional photographer like me, you want to do everything in your power to enhance the "money" shots.

Together, these two features add at least a hundred dollars to the quality / value of every camera and lens I purchase from now on. Doubly awesome, because there's no risk of this software getting stolen, dropped in the field, or any of the other perils that come with owning expensive objects.

While OpticsPro does offer some small ability to manage your photos, I highly recommend combining it with Adobe Lightroom - it even has a plugin to integrate directly with Lightroom: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00VWCKJVA/ref=as_li_tl?ie=UTF8&camp=1789&creative=390957&creativeASIN=B00VWCKJVA&linkCode=as2&tag=todmedblo-20&linkId=SMWKR6FG4HMUEGKE

The Carbonite back up rep yesterday basically let me think I had Alzheimer because he said there was no file by that name in that folder for the last 30 days per the Carbonite back up.  Today, I showed the Carbonite rep the DISQUS comment page where I copy/pasted part of the file that is lost and it says it was posted 15 days ago.  I told him everything copied here is exactly what the file folder has in it and can't we look for that phrase or this phrase. NO.   I thought the file had the name LIST in it so we looked through 1700 files with LIST in it from 2008 2010 2011 to 2015 all years mixed up not in order.   It took forever.  For every word you "guess" the file name is named...this is what you have to do. Finally, the rep said since I knew exactly the date the file was correct, he would bump it up and hopefully another rep could find my file.   I recreated it using my copied DISQUS comments and if I had not posted it, I would never have my file back.     Carbonite when "searching' cannot sort by date.  If you search APPLE it bring up every year the word APPLE is mentioned as a FILE NAME or FOLDER NAME when you know you need to search only 15 May 2015 for the word APPLE.  I've had Carbonite for 5 years.  My last 2 yearcontact is up in 2016 and I won't renew but will go with another company or just back it up with my own external drive.

text:
review_headline: Buyer be warned about this faulty product. Look at the number of one star reviews versus five star. That says it all.
review_body: I was forced to order Quickbooks Pro 2015 because when using my 2012 version I was getting notice that I would not be able to use online banking after May 31, 2015. I ordered and downloaded the software through the Intuit website. Upon trying to open the program, it would start and then automatically close after about a minute and a half, as if it was timing out. I called customer service and dealt with them all day yesterday. They elevated me to "level 2" (if there really is such a thing) and after several hours of attempting to fix the problem, NOTHING. I was on the phone for over four hours when the tech told me I could hang up as he would continue to work remotely on my computer. In a follow up phone call he told me he couldn't get it running and he would be sending it to "triage" and that someone else would call me the next day. I asked if he could at least reactivate my 2012 version to which he said he would. HOWEVER, now that doesn't work either. It had worked perfectly well before. It is doing the same thing that the 2015 version was doing. I have not received a call yet, and it being the end of the month when checks have to be printed and invoices have to be sent out, my business has come to a screeching halt. I may be elevating my concern over this product to legal council. This is unacceptable, especially after a customer has laid out $200 for the supposed necessary "Upgrade."  UPDATE: Eventually the "triage" person called me and started off by telling me that he wanted me to understand that the problem was not the software, but instead the problem was in my computer. I told him that was nonsense because my previous version of Quickbooks 2012 was working just fine. HE THREATENED TO HANG UP ON ME. I relented and told him yes the problem was in my computer. Quickbooks 2015 was in my computer and THAT was the problem. He went on to work on the software and after several more hours finally got it to work. While I am now satisfied, there is no way that this much effort should have had to go into making the "upgraded" product work. My computer had met all the requirements to run QB2015. There is clearly something wrong with the product as evidenced by the proportion of 1 star to 5 star reviews being given.

text:
review_headline: Widespread user requests to resolve "Operations in Progress" issue still not resolved review_body: This review also appears under the 3-license package listing.

I upgraded from the 2014 version to the 2015 release, trusting comments by Acronis representatives on this site that a longstanding problem, known as the "Operations in Progress bug," had finally been resolved. As a retired IT manager, I realize that fixes require time, and I am more patient than most.

The "Operations in Progress" behavior prevents Windows users from properly shutting down their machines. While the Acronis site states that this is short-term, necessary behavior for its application to complete processing, in fact, it will lock the shutdown process indefinitely. For a full description of the problem, and the simple kinds of coding changes Acronis could have made to fix it, go to my review of the 2014 product at http://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/R1TT0JA4FRFOLM/ref=cm_cr_pr_viewpnt?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B00EFRMBA6#R1TT0JA4FRFOLM.

The software behaved differently for a few months following the 2015 release's installation in November 2014, in that the "Operations in Progress" message usually timed out. But then, it abruptly changed back to the behavior so disliked in the 2014 release, always stopping the shutdown indefinitely. This tells me that not only has the problem not been fixed, but it certainly appears that Acronis altered the software without public notice a few months into this release. Any company that treats its customers with due respect will (a) listen to widespread concerns, and fix them; and (b) not apply updates without the customer's knowledge. However, Acronis projects an impression of corporate stubbornness and arrogance.

For a company that announced a billion-dollar (with a "b") revenue goal in March 2014, there is no excuse. Staffing should not be an issue. And the fixes should take only a few man-hours of coding time (if that), provided the software was written intelligently in the first place. Isuspect the staff who reported to me could complete them in less than an hour.

The "Operations in Progress" problem continues to mess up Windows updates, many of which depend upon an orderly shutdown process that is not blocked by a third-party application like Acronis.

I am researching reviews for other backup options. I am impatient to move away from Acronis's products and its disrespect of customers. star_rating: 1 review_id: R2RLJPEZWFQNI6

text:
review_headline: WriteWay Pro is the right way to go!
review_body: I've been using my WriteWay Professional software for more than a year now and I really love it. Out of curiosity I tried a couple of other writing programs, such as the "Ultimate" EBook Creator (which it isn't, even though it's double the price), and none I've seen so far compares to WriteWay Pro. WWP is polished, professional, a great organizational tool, and helps the writer build and develop his material in a coherent, smooth and uncomplicated manner, from the earliest idea stage to the finished product, submission stage.  Unlike some programs (such as Ultimate EBook Creator, etc.), WWP can be accessed without an internet connection, and without signing in with registration numbers, etc. every time you want to work on your book, which should be true of all writing software, but isn't. With WWP, you can work on your creative projects, any time and anywhere, without privacy concerns that the software designer may be looking over your shoulder as you write. WriteWay's developers made WWP very user friendly and their customer service is wonderful. WWP won't spam you with annoying personal emails, like that other ebook program, but they're there when you need them.  PROS: * Create as many books as you like at the same time (and there’s even a section for future book ideas) * Preview your in-progress work in a number of ways, including “Listen” as your computer reads your work back to you; also preview in draft, galley, manuscript and publish ready forms * Export files to Rich Text Files (RTF), Hypertext Markup Language (HTML), Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF), Microsoft Word Format 97-2003 (*.doc), and Microsoft Word Format (*.docx), making it easy to upload and electronically publish your own content at Amazon.com in Kindle and BN.com in NOOK formats * Front Matter section for Cover Page, Dedication, Foreword - and User Page for extras * Import book chapters * Folders to organize your research (and you can add any file you have on your computer toyour research folders) * Character Profiles to help you people your story with unique personalities (includes suggestions you may use to help you get a better feel of your characters) * Auto save option automatically saves your work at set intervals, as well as intervals you determine * Dictionaries include English (both US and UK), German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch and Portuguese * Spell check * Optional first line auto indent and preferable “smart quotes” (curly quotation marks)  * Easily import and imbed images into your projects * Bullets and numbering options * Single, 1.5 and double spacing * Notecards, storyboards, ruler options * Word count * Word count tracking * Word usage analysis lets you know when to consult your thesaurus for overused words * Table of contents to publish-ready exports * Search lets you search a scene, a chapter or your entire book for a word or phrase * Extensive “Help” section guides you through everything you need to know to use WriteWay Pro to its full advantage and make you a successful writer! * AUTOMATIC UPDATES (when you go online and open WriteWay Pro) will ensure you always have the latest version (you have the option to accept or decline updates too)  CONS: * It won’t type your manuscript for you - you'll still have to do the hard stuff, but WriteWay Pro makes the hard stuff easier!  I have many good things to say about WWP, but best thing I can say about it is it's so well done, and such a pleasure to use, it actually inspires me to write! And P.S. The price is great, too.

I am in a race with another individual to see who can crank out a reasonable first draft of a screenplay first. As I have begun to look at the tool bar and explore what is really lurking behind the curtain, I see many wizard type tools that will be fun to explore. Character arc is one of those. Outlining is another, except that it is taking a beating by some reviewers. I like to outline separately from the software anyway.

review_headline: NINE REASONS TO WITHHOLD PURCHASE review_body: I gave a one star rating to get your attention. It's two stars at best, however, I see I'm far from alone here!

As of 05/02/2015 I purchased the latest version of the Avanquest Bookkeeper Software. I was quite disappointed. Be forewarned that:

1. This program has severe limitations in templates
2. Output options for printed documents are deeply limited
3. Graphics options for personalization are extremely limited; probably because they want you to buy the logo software program they also sell
4. Workflow has a printing glitch; printing is delayed by a "make selection" screen that halts your workflow, then sort of 'reboots' before giving a final printing option. This is very, very annoying, as you'll see. It doesn’t allow you to print the document on the screen before you, so if you just edited something, you can't tell which version will print
5. THIS PROGRAM IS NOT INTUITIVE NOR USER FRIENDLY. It may have a simple user interface, but the LEARNING CURVE IS STEEP due to poor design
6. You will have two Help options for this program other than customer support (see below). The first is the Help Topics sub-program, which is entirely minimal and inflexible. It is useless. You will learn this program by trial-and-error. The second is the FAQ online option at www.avanquest.com. The Help menus here are more extensive and informative, but frustrating in the event you aren't familiar with the program to begin with (pick your poison!).
7. I purchased the latest build and version of Bookkeeper directly from Avanquest, v. 11.0.0.4 Two weeks later, I discover there are listings for versions 14x and 15x, but they are not accessible
at the Avanquest website.
8. Do no expect discount options on future upgrades. Besides, you won't want one.

**9. Above all else, be warned: there are neither free customer support nor direct contact options other than by e-mail. Tech Support costs $10.00 - $20.00 out of the box, AND you will definitely need Tech Support. This accounts for the program's low initial cost, [and] even though they're taking your money again, be prepared to "hurry up and wait.”

One caveat: www.http://accounting-software-review.toptenreviews.com/small-business/bookkeeper-review.html reviews many buying options BUT will not warn you about serious program flaws. Read as much as you can elsewhere.

Final word: I use Intuit for its merchant services, with which I am quite pleased. I bought Bookkeeper out of desperation and was somewhat prepared for it to be a throwaway or tax write-off. It has succeeded. Based on reviews I've read, and my personal experience with Intuit as a vendor, I strongly urge you to make the Intuit Quickbooks purchase. Tax accountants love it. There are both “cloud” rental and one-time ownership purchase options if you desire.
